diagnosis: Familial adenomatous polyposis–associated cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma
legend: The multifocal thyroid carcinomas in familial adenomatous polyposis are those of cribriform-modular thyroid carcinoma. The cribriform component is usually admixed with morulae. Morulae are positive for CK5 (as shown here) and CD5 and are negative for p63, p40, thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF1), and PAX8.

diagnosis: Familial adenomatous polyposis–associated cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma
legend: The morula cells immunostain for CD5 in a membranous pattern. The scattered CD5-positive T cells are also stained.

diagnosis: Familial adenomatous polyposis–associated cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma
legend: This tumour type, whether or not associated with familial adenomatous polyposis, shows absent staining for thyroglobulin by the tumour cells.

diagnosis: Familial adenomatous polyposis–associated cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma
legend: Another characteristic of the cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma is the strong nuclear and cytoplasmic expression of β-catenin by the tumour cells.

Typical cribriform-morular carcinomas are easily recognized under low-power microscopy. A combination of morular, trabecular, solid, follicular, and spindled patterns of growth can be identified. The cribriform architecture is formed by anastomosing bars or arches 1–2 cell layers thick, and the morular component has peculiar nuclear inclusions.
